reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to assess whether pembrolizumab engaged PD-1 or epacadostat engaged IDO1. Cannot determine if targets were hit. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to assess whether checkpoint blockade or tryptophan catabolism pathways were modulated. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoints clearly failed - PFS HR 1.00 (p=0.51711) and OS rate at 6 months HR 1.13 (p=0.80666) showed no benefit for the combination vs pembrolizumab alone. The combination arm performed essentially identically to the control arm. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Trial appears adequately powered (n=706) and duration was appropriate (104 weeks). Safety profile was similar between arms with no dose-limiting toxicity preventing adequate dosing. This appears to be a clean failure of the combination hypothesis.

failure_modes.evidence: No biomarker data available to determine where in the causal chain the failure occurred - cannot assess target engagement or pathway modulation for either pembrolizumab or epacadostat
